events.title: The London Carthusian martyrs
events.shortBlurb: The first blood of the English Reformation was shed at Tyburn when three monastic priors refused the royal supremacy…
body: On 4 May 1535, John Houghton, prior of the London Charterhouse, together with Robert Lawrence, prior of Beauvale, and Augustine Webster, prior of Axholme, were dragged to Tyburn and put to death. With them died the Bridgettine monk Richard Reynolds and the parish priest John Haile.

Their crime was refusal to swear the Oath of Supremacy by which Henry VIII made himself head of the Church in England. They were hanged, cut down still living, and disemboweled — the protomartyrs of the long English persecution. Houghton and several of his brethren were later numbered among the Forty Martyrs of England and Wales, canonized in 1970.
